correctness.rationale: The source pair-approximation selection gradient, assumed as an established premise, is proportional to (n+2)B'(nx)-nc. For B as sum of two logistic stage benefits, direct differentiation yields g(z+h)+g(z-h)=(1+H cosh z)/(H+cosh z)^2 with H=cosh h, z=beta n(x-1/2). For C=cosh z in [1,Q], F_H(C)=(1+HC)/(H+C)^2 has derivative (H²−2−HC)/(H+C)^3. When H>2 it increases until C*=H−2/H then strictly decreases; since Q>H>C*, exactly two admissible C roots require theta strictly between both endpoint values and the maximum. Each C>1 gives two interior x, total four. Quadratic formula gives C± and stability alternates by sign of derivative. At attracting roots B''(nx)<0 and the explicit positive coefficient in source invasion-curvature Eq B18 gives ESS. Independent direct sigmoid derivative evaluation and four-root bisections reproduced exact example and signs. This is exact in the approximation, not in finite stochastic networks.

final_claim: In the weak-selection pair-approximation one-dimensional public-goods investment dynamics with two equally steep increasing sigmoid benefit stages at symmetric thresholds, there are exactly four interior singular investments iff H=cosh h>2 and max{1/(H+1),(1+H Q)/(H+Q)^2}<theta<H^2/[4(H^2-1)], with Q=cosh(beta n/2), theta=nc/[(n+2)b beta]. Two of the four are local convergence-attractors and evolutionary-stability maxima; other two are repellers. The sharp threshold separation is beta(T+−T−)>2 acosh 2.
